claims.text: Deliberate compositional tuning can tune the magnetic behavior of a non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy.
Deliberate compositional tuning can tune the magnetocaloric behavior of a non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy.
Increasing the Ti fraction accentuates antiferromagnetic coupling.
Enhanced antiferromagnetic coupling reduces saturation magnetization.
A reduction in saturation magnetization alters magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Altered magnetocrystalline anisotropy tunes the magnetocaloric effect by changing the balance of magnetic energy terms governing phase transitions.
FeCoNiTi can be prepared in both equiatomic and non-equiatomic compositions.
The proposed FeCoNiTi-like baseline has a predominantly fcc structure.
FeCoNiTi exhibits magnetic phase transitions over a broad temperature range.
Increasing Ti produces atomic-scale local modifications in the electronic and magnetic environment.
An equiatomic or as-cast baseline has higher saturation magnetization than the proposed Ti-modified compositions.
An equiatomic or as-cast baseline has a fixed magnetocaloric response.
Changing Ti content will produce a systematic reduction in saturation magnetization.
Changing Ti content will shift or enhance the magnetic entropy change near magnetic phase transitions.
Large compositional changes can generate additional phases that independently affect magnetic or magnetocaloric properties.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes both increasing and decreasing Ti, but the proposed mediator is specifically attributed to increased Ti, while the predicted systematic trend is described broadly for increasing deviations from equiatomic composition without distinguishing the direction of Ti change.
